clue.text: Parts of the body designed to bear swords?

definitions.text: Parts of the body designed to bear swords?

parts.words: Parts of the body designed to bear swords?
parts.note: read literally, the flat bones at the top of the back sound like places made for carrying weapons, since a blade is a sword

explanation.definitionFit: These flat triangular bones at the upper back are body parts whose name contains a word for swords, so the clue jokes they were made to carry them.

clue.text: Croatian lost time fighting this player

indicators.note: fighting suggests the remaining letters scrapping and tumbling into a new order
lost tells us the word Croatian drops one of its letters

explanation.surface: A Croatian soldier gave up his instrument once war broke out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes T from CROATIAN, leaving CROAIAN, and 'fighting' rearranges those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This small egg-shaped wind instrument is something that plays music, so a player in the sense of an instrument.

clue.text: Both sides welcome first-class accommodation in the wild

indicators.note: to welcome is to take someone in, so the two side letters enclose the next piece

parts.note: left and right, abbreviated L
the second side, right, abbreviated R
A1 means first-class, written AI with the one as I

explanation.surface: Every party is pleased to see top-quality housing in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Both sides' gives L and R (left and right), which 'welcome' AI between them; A1 for first-class is written with I for 1.
explanation.definitionFit: A den is the home of a wild animal, its shelter out in nature.

clue.text: Supplied crack in deep disguise

indicators.note: in places the joke inside the rearranged letters
disguise means the letters of deep are changed in appearance by being reordered

parts.note: a crack is a witty remark, a quip

explanation.surface: A joke is hidden deep within a masquerade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' looks like a split, but here it is a wisecrack; 'disguise' rearranges the letters of 'deep' to EPED, and 'in' wraps that around the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Being furnished with what is needed is to be provided or kitted out.

clue.text: Clouded over early after bright start

indicators.note: after places the scrambled word behind the opening letter
start means only the opening letter of bright is used
over in the sense of knocked over, so the letters of early are turned about

explanation.surface: The weather turned cloudy early after a sunny beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clouded' is the eyes, not the sky; 'start' takes the first letter of 'bright', and 'over' rearranges 'early' into LEARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes that are dim and blurred, from tiredness, are said to be clouded.

clue.text: Acknowledgements from delegations after a day

indicators.note: after puts the groups of envoys behind the opening letters

parts.note: delegations are groups of envoys sent abroad, missions

explanation.surface: Diplomatic thank-yous arrive once the visiting envoys have had a day.
explanation.definitionFit: Confessions or concessions that something is true are acknowledgements.

clue.text: The compiler went up to university with recent copy

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading the word from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: the setter refers to himself, so the compiler is me
recent means late, as in the late news

explanation.surface: The crossword setter arrived at college with a fresh imitation.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter calls himself 'The compiler', giving ME, which 'went up' turns into EM in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate someone, matching what they do, is to copy them.

clue.text: Resist changes in coinage with tenacity

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the coins

parts.note: pence are British coins, coinage

indicators.note: changes says the letters of resist are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Fight off any alteration to the currency with stubborn determination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges 'Resist' into ERSIST; 'coinage' means British pence, which wrap round it after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding on stubbornly and refusing to give up is the quality called tenacity.

clue.text: A numeric sort of digital improvement

indicators.note: sort as in sort out, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A sort of mathematical upgrade to a digital system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' looks like computers, but digits are fingers: the treatment improves the nails.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic treatment of the hands and nails tidies up the fingers, which are digits.

clue.text: Short time employment for computer worker

parts.note: a mo, short for moment, is a short time
employment of something is its use

explanation.surface: A brief spell of work for someone in IT.
explanation.walkthrough: 'computer worker' suggests a person, but it is the hand-held device that operates a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: The small hand-held pointing device is a tool that works a computer's cursor.

clue.text: Waspish couple reportedly got fruit

parts.note: waspish means irritable, easily annoyed, prickly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said or heard, so the word for a couple is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: a couple is two, a pair

explanation.surface: An irritable pair of people ended up with some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: PAIR (couple) sounds like PEAR, as 'reportedly' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: The edible fruit of a cactus of the Opuntia genus.

clue.text: Runs to help in attack

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
aid means help

explanation.surface: Runs are brought on to support an offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden assault on a place is an attack.

clue.text: Vehicles that leave marks of injury on bear

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece on another follows it

parts.note: to bear something such as a badge is to wear or sport it
scars are the marks an injury leaves

explanation.surface: Cars that leave a bear with marks of injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' looks like the animal, but it is the verb, as in to bear a badge, meaning sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast low-slung two-seater cars built for speed are vehicles.

clue.text: Ethnic group studies Ascot, for example

parts.note: a race is an ethnic group
a course is a programme of studies

explanation.surface: A group of people of one ethnicity studies Ascot as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is a famous horse-racing venue in Berkshire, England, so 'for example' marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is an example of a track where horses race, the British venue of the Royal meeting.

clue.text: The cleaning lady has a dress, oddly, for these word games

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a cleaning lady

indicators.note: oddly means the odd-numbered letters of dress are taken: first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: The cleaner wears a strange outfit for party games.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAR is British slang for a cleaning lady; 'oddly' takes D, E, S from 'dress'.
explanation.definitionFit: Party guessing games where words are acted out in mime are known by this name.

clue.text: Extends studies on central London area

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece on another comes after it

parts.note: W1 is the postcode district for central London, written WI with the one as I
dens are studies, rooms for private work

explanation.surface: Someone extends their studies about the centre of London.
explanation.walkthrough: W1 is a postcode in the West End of London; the 1 becomes I, and 'on' puts DENS after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To broaden or make something wider is to extend it.

clue.text: Cold call about a note supplying the necessaries

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cold-and-call pieces go round the rest

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps
to ring is to call someone on the phone
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A cold phone call about a note on what is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: TE is a note of the sol-fa scale (do, re, mi...); 'about' puts A plus that note between the C and the word for call.
explanation.definitionFit: Providing food and drink, and other requirements, for an event is supplying what is needed.

clue.text: Miss the old flipping footman!

parts.note: to miss something is to lack it

indicators.note: flipping means the archaic word is turned over and read backwards

parts.note: ye is an old form of the

explanation.surface: Missing the old footman, curse him!
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild swear word, but it turns YE (old 'the') into EY.
explanation.definitionFit: A servant in livery, a footman, is a servile attendant.

clue.text: One's in the soup after Tory accepted resounding defeat

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so the Tory abbreviation surrounds the defeat

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, a Tory
a rout is a crushing, resounding defeat

explanation.surface: A Conservative is in trouble after conceding a heavy election loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the soup' suggests trouble, but here it is literal: a crisp cube of bread served in soup.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cube of fried bread is something that floats in a bowl of broth.

clue.text: Left home in American state — to take drugs!

indicators.note: in places the two short pieces inside the American state

parts.note: Maine is a state in the north-east of the USA
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone left home in an American state to inject drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'home' is a crossword convention for IN, as in staying in; 'in' then puts L and that word inside the north-eastern US state.
explanation.definitionFit: To inject a narcotic straight into a vein is slang for using drugs.

clue.text: Road up on favourite American drive

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the road name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the M1 is a British motorway, written MI with the one as I
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A road being dug up is the main concern for a favourite American car journey.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway; written MI and turned 'up' it gives IM.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the drive or momentum that keeps something moving.

clue.text: A French source of water that makes you sick

parts.note: un is French for a
a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: A French spring whose water makes you ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ill is being sick.

clue.text: Beaten by argument in favour of being put forward

parts.note: a pro is an argument in favour of something, as in pros and cons
pounded means beaten

explanation.surface: Someone thrashed by a supporting argument is pushed forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To propose a theory for consideration is to put it forward.

clue.text: Large-scale source of power in melting ice

indicators.note: in places the first letter of power inside the remelted ice
melting suggests the ice losing its shape, so its letters change order
source of means the first letter, the point where the word begins

explanation.surface: A huge power source is found in melting ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'melting' rearranges ICE to EIC, and 'in' puts P from 'source of power' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on a grand, heroic scale, such as a film, is called this.

clue.text: Three points about river bird

indicators.note: about means going round, so the compass points surround the river

parts.note: west, east and north are three compass points, W, E, N

explanation.surface: A bird perched where three paths meet near a river.
explanation.walkthrough: W, E and N are compass points; 'about' puts R between the W and the E.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny brown songbird with a cocked tail.

clue.text: Player's answer to put in credit

indicators.note: put in tells us the little word is placed inside the credit abbreviation

explanation.surface: A musician's answer is to put something on account.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Player' with ''s' as 'is'; 'put in' places the word 'to' inside the credit abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer on stage plays a role, so a player is a performer.

clue.text: Leave after disagreement about missing ends

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Leave after disagreement about missing ends (8)' for EMIGRATE: no parse found; the letters are TIME + RAGE anagrammed but no clue words supply them, so the clue looks garbled
annotationWithheld.clue: Leave after disagreement about missing ends

clue.text: Einstein tag ill suits them — not!

definitions.text: Einstein tag ill suits them — not!

indicators.note: suits is read as an anagram signal, the letters being dressed up in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The intellectual label would hardly fit Einstein badly, so the joke is that it suits such thinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of EINSTEIN TAG ILL spells the class of intellectuals; '— not!' tells us the label in fact suits them well.
explanation.definitionFit: The intellectual elite of a society, the thinkers to whom Einstein belongs.
